points.why: It says tracing correctly only shows internal consistency, that a tidy diagram can be wrong, and that the polish makes it look more trustworthy than it is.
It recommends review by customer success, support and sales, but not reading each loop aloud to the owners of each link or treating a wince as a wrong or missing link.
It separates the archetype label from the trace, gives the canonical quick-fix-with-delayed-backfiring-side-effect definition, and asks the user to name the specific fix and delay.
It says the polish hides that each arrow is a guess and that a confident diagram can mislead the board.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly questions the Fixes That Fail label instead of accepting it from the polarity check.
